title: Greetings from the Rainforest
text:
Dear Uncle Ben,

Hello from the rainforest! It rained {number} times today, and every drop was as big as a {noun}. Our guide, Rosa, showed us a tiny frog that was bright {color}. She says it sings {adverb} every night.

Yesterday we crossed a rope bridge. A monkey sat in the middle and would not move until I gave him my {plural noun}. Then he {past tense verb} and swung away.

Our hotel is a treehouse. My bed is a {adjective} hammock, and a parrot outside my window says "{silly word}" every morning. Breakfast is bananas and {plural noun}.

Tomorrow we will {verb} down the river in a canoe. I hope I see a sloth {verb ending in ing}!

Your nephew,
Sam
P.S. Please water my {adjective} plant and say hi to the {noun}.

title: What to Pack for the Jungle
text:
Going on a jungle trip? Here is what every explorer needs to pack.

First, bring a raincoat and a pair of {adjective} boots. The jungle is very muddy, and the mud likes to {verb}. Next, pack a flashlight, a water bottle, and {number} {plural noun}. You never know when you might need them.

Do not forget bug spray! Jungle mosquitoes are small but very {adjective}. My cousin forgot his bug spray last year, and he {past tense verb} the whole week.

You should also pack a hat, a map, and a {noun}. The monkeys are not allowed to have {food}, but they will ask {adverb} anyway. Bring extra {plural noun} for the toucans. Wear your hat on your {body part}.

Last of all, pack a notebook so you can draw every {noun} you see. Happy {verb ending in ing}!

title: Explorer's Journal, Day Three
text:
Day three in the jungle. I woke up at sunrise because a toucan was {verb ending in ing} on my tent. I gave him a {noun}, and he flew away happy.

After breakfast, Professor Plum and I hiked to the Great Waterfall. We found a giant flower that smelled exactly like {food}. Professor Plum wrote it down in her {adjective} notebook.

At the waterfall, a family of monkeys was taking a bath. The baby monkey {past tense verb} so {adverb} that we all laughed. Then he tossed {number} {plural noun} into the water.

Tonight we are camping by the river. Professor Plum says the frogs here can {verb} better than any frog in the world. For dinner we had rice and {plural noun}, cooked {adverb} over the fire. I am trying to stay awake, but I am very {adjective}.

Tomorrow we will look for the rare purple {noun}.

title: Jungle News: The Big Parrot Parade
text:
This is Jungle Radio with today's top story.

The Big Parrot Parade happened this morning by the river. More than {number} parrots marched in a line, each one wearing a tiny {noun} on its head. Captain Feathers, the oldest parrot in the jungle, flew {adverb} at the front and shouted "{exclamation}!" every few minutes.

Next came the toucans, who played drums with their {plural noun}. A group of frogs followed, {verb ending in ing} as loudly as they could. The monkeys threw {plural noun} instead of flowers.

"This is the most {adjective} parade ever," said Mrs. Leaf, a tree frog. "Next year I hope they will {verb} even more."

The parade ended at the big mango tree, where everyone ate {food} and {past tense verb} until sunset. The prize for best hat went to a {adjective} sloth wearing a {noun}. Back to you, {name}!

title: Rules for the Treehouse Hotel
text:
Welcome to the Treehouse Hotel, the tallest hotel in the jungle! Please follow these rules.

Our elevator is a basket on a rope. Please ride it {adverb} and keep your {body part} inside at all times.

Breakfast is served on the top branch at eight o'clock. Today we are having {adjective} mangoes and {plural noun}. Do not share your food with the monkeys. Last week a guest did, and the monkeys {past tense verb} on her table.

Quiet time starts after dinner. Please do not {verb} in the hallways. The sloth in Room 4 has been trying to fall asleep since {noun} Day.

Every room has a {adjective} hammock, a clean towel, and a {noun}. If you need help, ring the bell and a parrot will come {verb ending in ing}.

If you see a snake in your room, do not worry. His name is Steve, and he is just looking for his {color} hat and his {plural noun}. We hope your visit is {adjective}!

title: Toucan's Famous Fruit Salad
text:
Tilly the Toucan makes the best fruit salad in the jungle. Here is her secret recipe.

You will need two bananas, one mango, a bowl of berries, and a {adjective} coconut. You will also need {number} {plural noun}, but only fresh ones.

First, ask a monkey to help you {verb} the bananas. Monkeys are very good at this. Then cut the mango into the shape of a {noun}.

Next, put the fruit in a big bowl and stir it {adverb} with your beak. If you do not have a beak, use a {noun}. Add a sprinkle of {food} on top. Tilly says this makes it taste {adjective}.

Let the salad sit in the sun while you are {verb ending in ing}. If it {past tense verb} while you were gone, that is normal.

Serve it in a bowl shaped like a {body part} and wait for your friends to say, "{exclamation}!"

title: Talking with a Sloth
text:
Our reporter, Jada, spent the whole day with Sid the Sloth. It took a while.

Jada: What does a normal day look like for you?
Sid: I wake up at noon. Then I hang upside down and think about {plural noun}. After that, I take a {adjective} nap.

Jada: What is your favorite food?
Sid: Leaves, mostly. But on my birthday I have a {adjective} cake made of {food}.

Jada: Do you ever hurry?
Sid: Once. I heard someone was giving away free {plural noun}, so I moved {adverb}. It only took me {number} hours to get there.

Jada: What do you do for fun?
Sid: I like {verb ending in ing} with my best friend, a turtle named Gus. Last week we {past tense verb} together.

Jada: Any advice for our readers?
Sid: Yes. Slow down, take time to {verb}, and always keep a {noun} in your fur. Also, never {verb} in a {adjective} tree.

title: Help Wanted: Jungle Tour Guide
text:
Help wanted! Jungle Fun Tours needs a new tour guide.

You must love animals, walking, and {plural noun}. You must be able to {verb} while carrying a big backpack. It also helps if you are {adjective} in the morning.

Every day, you will lead visitors down the jungle trail. You will point out the parrots, the frogs, and the famous dancing {noun}. When visitors get tired, you will cheer them up by {verb ending in ing}.

The best part of this job is lunch by the waterfall: rice, beans, and {plural noun}. The hardest part is the monkeys. They like to grab your hat and your {noun}. Just say "{silly word}" {adverb}, and they will give them back.

You get one day off each week and a free {color} shirt. Our last guide loved this job so much that she {past tense verb} every day. To apply, send us a drawing of yourself next to a {adjective} {noun}.

title: The Jungle Talent Show
text:
Attention, all jungle animals! The Jungle Talent Show is this Saturday at the Big Rock by the river. The show starts when the frogs stop {verb ending in ing}. Please bring a blanket and a {noun} to sit on.

Here are some of the acts. The Monkey Brothers will {verb} on one hand while eating bananas. Lola the Leopard will sing a {adjective} song about {plural noun}. Then the elephant will play the trumpet with her {body part}.

The judges are an owl, a tortoise, and a very {adjective} anteater. The winner gets a golden coconut and {number} {plural noun}.

Snacks will be sold by the parrots. Please pay {adverb}, and do not let the parrots count the money. Last year they {past tense verb} and nobody knew what anything cost.

The show ends with everyone dancing to a song about a {noun}. See you there, and please wear something {adjective}!

title: A Letter from the River Boat
text:
Dear Grandpa,

I am writing from a boat on the jungle river. Captain Diaz lets me steer for {number} minutes every afternoon. Yesterday I steered us right into a {noun}, but nobody minded.

The river is wide and brown and very {adjective}. Pink dolphins swim next to our boat. When I wave, they {past tense verb} and splash me.

Every night we eat dinner on the deck. The cook makes rice, beans, and a soup made of {plural noun}. Tonight a monkey climbed aboard and tried to {verb} with our spoons. Captain Diaz shooed him away {adverb}.

My bed is a hammock that smells like {food}. At bedtime the frogs sing. They sound like {plural noun} {verb ending in ing} in the rain. I will bring you back a {adjective} surprise.

Love,
Maya
P.S. Please tell the cat I said "{exclamation}!" and give her a {noun}.
